findings.summary: The core is the densest region of both contour panels and the place the caption makes its claim (four maxima), but at the rendered 1399x720 size the six shared levels of two series converge there and the solved contour spacing falls to roughly one pixel: a strict-blue run-length scan over a 100x110 px core window gives a median run of 3 px and a maximum of 27 px, with 3 per cent of runs at or above 10 px. The lines do stand apart, so this does not hold the figure, but a reader cannot count the four maxima at a glance and must zoom to check the caption's claim.

Same defect as the 137D poloidal panel, and slightly denser: over the same core window the strict-blue run lengths have a median of 2 px and a maximum of 26 px, with 4 per cent of runs at or above 10 px, so the caption's 'three main-plasma maxima and a local minimum' is marked in the panel but not countable at the rendered size.

The MAST panel autoscales to roughly 0.47-0.58 MA/m2 while the two DIII-D panels run 0 to about 2.3 and 2.5, so a variation of about twenty per cent is drawn as a full-height arch beside peaks eight times larger. The caption now declares that this panel has its own density scale, which is what keeps the figure honest, but the three columns are still read by height at a glance and the mismatch invites over-reading MAST's shoulder enhancement.

method: Every verdict below is read from the six rendered PNGs attached to this review (1399x720 each), opened directly. Only two script files were read, to anchor findings and to explain a marker vocabulary: scripts/prototypes/diiid_hollow_current/render.py at the reviewed head, and the fragment's rendered captions. No SVG source was opened, read or rendered, and no image other than the six named PNGs was opened. Two numeric checks were run on the rasters themselves: an outer-border ink scan (a clipped-text check) and a strict-blue run-length scan across the contour cores. Both are reported where they bear on a verdict.
